guard_streams.source: UK home broadband performance, measurement period March 2023
guard_streams.write_limit: The study measures a volunteer router panel and provider-supplied package data. National or panel performance cannot be written as a measurement for a selected parcel outside the tested panel.

facts.detail: Ofcom published the March 2023 home-broadband performance report on 14 September 2023.
The report is based on data collected in March 2023.
The research covers fixed-line broadband delivered to UK homes.
The accompanying market context states 86% of UK households use fixed broadband.
One data source is SamKnows volunteers using hardware monitoring units connected to routers.
The second source is data from the UK's four largest broadband providers.
A technical report was published with the study.
Ofcom published supporting annexes.
Ofcom published chart data as CSV.
Ofcom published panellist data as CSV.

guard_streams.source: Latest home broadband performance trends revealed
guard_streams.write_limit: These are aggregate findings from a monitored customer panel and provider data. They are not selected-parcel availability, live orderability or a parcel-specific speed test.

facts.detail: Ofcom published the trends article on 14 September 2023.
Average home-broadband download speed was 69.4 Mbit/s in March 2023.
The average download speed increased 17% year on year.
Eighty-eight percent of lines received a 24-hour average of at least 30 Mbit/s.
Three percent of connections averaged less than 10 Mbit/s over 24 hours.
Average upload speed reached 18.4 Mbit/s.
Average upload speed increased 73% year on year.
Peak-time averages were 70.3 Mbit/s urban and 56.0 Mbit/s rural.
Cable connections averaged 270.6 Mbit/s download.
Full-fibre connections averaged 149.2 Mbit/s download.
